newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Alcatel sees big leap in ADSL sales.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel sees big leap in ADSL sales.

text.p: French telecoms equipment group Alcatel Alsthom expects revenue from ADSL (Asymmetric Digital Subcriber Line) technology to reach almost one billion French francs by 2000, a senior official said on Tuesday.

"We are expecting something like 150 million French francs this year and to grow and more than triple in the coming year," Martin De Prycker, Alcatel's vice president for access systems division told Reuters.
"We are expecting close to one billion French francs by year 2000," he said.
ADSL technology allows high-speed access to the Internet and other interactive services while maintaining existing telephone copper-wiring infrastructure.
De Prycker was hosting a news conference in Singapore on Alcatel's partnership with modem maker Hayes Microcomputer Products Inc to supply ADSL products.
Alcatel officials were participating in the Asia Telecom 97 trade fair in Singapore.
